Subject: Vertex Retail — perf SLA & benchmark methodology alignment

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Business goals we heard: low-latency responses for the checkout microflow (chat/assist) with p95 latency at or below 250ms, support for sustained concurrency up to 200 sessions with short spikes to 500, and streaming support for partial responses for product recommendations.

2) Proposed Redwood SLO targets for initial qualification (we can adjust after the benchmark run):
   - p50 latency target: 60–80ms (token generation only)
   - p95 latency target: <= 250ms (end‑to‑end request)
   - sustained concurrency target: 200 concurrent active sessions
   - peak concurrency: bursts to 500 for 2–5 minutes
   - throughput target: ~80 req/s average for core checkout path
   - streaming chunk latency: initial chunk <= 120ms, subsequent chunks <= 70ms

3) Benchmark scope and asks from Vertex:
   - canonical prompt set for the checkout flow (we requested the internal prompts and a representative traffic mix)
   - sample production traces or replay logs for request size distribution and token counts
   - definition of success (business KPIs + acceptable quality delta vs current system)

4) Measurement & reproducibility: we recommended Redwood Harness v2.1 with seeded runs, canonical tokenization, and config checkpoints (model version, quantization, batch policy). I attached an initial prompt bundle (light sample) for discussion.

Attachments: [Attachment: initial_prompt_bundle.json (text/json)]

Next steps (proposed):
- Emily: share the canonical prompt set and a short replay (3–5k requests) by EOD Fri 7/2 — include any rate limits.
- Redwood: produce a measurement definition doc + run plan and a sample harness config by Tue 7/6.
- Schedule a 60-min joint run planning session w/ engineering and SRE — suggested slots Wed 7/7 or Thu 7/8.

If that looks right I’ll turn this into a short plan and HubSpot task.

Thanks,
Sergio

Thanks, Sergio — helpful recap. Confirming a few points from our side and adding clarifications so your run plan aligns with our environment: 

- We can deliver the canonical prompt set and a replay sample (CSV + JSON trace) by EOD Friday, 7/2. I’m attaching an early draft of the prompt pack for your review.
- Streaming requirement: product recommendations must stream as they are retrieved (we cannot wait for the full generation for the initial 1–2 suggestions). That makes the initial-chunk latency especially important.
- Traffic shape: our checkout conversations are short (average 12 tokens generated, 1–3 user turns) but high QPS during peak windows. For initial qualification assume steady-state 80 req/s and plan for spike windows up to 500 concurrent sessions for flash sales.
- Measurement ask: can you capture p25/p50/p90/p95/p99, tail percentiles for streaming chunk times, and CPU/GPU utilization during the run? We will want a CSV export and raw harness logs.

Attaching: vertex_prompt_set_v1.json (early)

Emily — great, thanks for the prompt pack. Below is the measurement definition and reproducibility checklist we’ll use for the qualification run. I’ll attach the Redwood eval spec (pdf) with the harness config examples and a minimal command-line recipe.

Measurement definitions (canonical):
- Request definition: user message + system instructions + model config. Tokenization normalization will use the same tokenizer binary we use in serving (BPE v1).
- Latency definitions:
   * generation_latency: time from model invocation to last token generated (ms)
   * response_latency: time from API ingress to final byte sent (ms)
   * chunk_latency: time from API ingress to first byte of streaming chunk (ms)
- Percentiles reported: p25, p50, p75, p90, p95, p99 for each latency metric; plus QPS and successful vs failed request ratio.
- Concurrency: measured as number of active sessions holding an open request/response stream. We will run steady-state profiles (200) and spike profiles (ramp 200->500 over 60s).
- Throughput: measured as completed responses per second excluding timeouts.

Reproducibility checklist (short):
1) Canonical prompt set (you provided v1) must be used without in-line personalization tokens unless explicitly documented.
2) Seed the RNG at the harness level and record seeds in run artifact.
3) Fix model binary/hash, quant config, and batch policy in a single run manifest.
4) Normalize tokenization and include per-request token counts in logs.
5) Provide a sample traffic mix (percentage of short/medium/long prompts).
6) Store raw harness logs + CSV summary (pcts + raw samples) in shared Drive folder for audit.

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot run:
- Redwood Harness run: two profiles (steady 1hr at 80 req/s w/ concurrency 200; spike test 30m with burst to 500)
- Single-model qualification using the suggested open checkpoint (we’ll propose 2 model variants: full FP16 and int8 quant)
- Reproducibility artifacts: seeds, harness config, run manifest, CSV exports, and raw logs.

Attachment: [Attachment: redwood_eval_spec_v2.pdf] — contains the harness config snippet, exact CLI commands (run-id capture), and CSV schema for exports.

If that matches your expectations we’ll draft an explicit run plan and share the HubSpot task. Also please confirm any IP/policy constraints for us storing anonymized traces in our S3 for troubleshooting.

—Marissa

Quick technical note from runtime side:
- For the streaming case we’ll validate two kernel profiles: the low-latency kernel (favor smaller batch sizes and preemptive KV cache warmup) and the throughput kernel (larger batching). We’ll pin the run manifest to the kernel selection we used.
- For int8 runs we’ll include a quantization profile and a small quality-check sub-run (1000 queries) to measure delta against fp16.
- If Vertex can share a 1–2 minute sample of production replay logs (sanitized) that captures the spike shape, it will help us set batching policies correctly rather than guessing.

Vivek
